front.title: MAP Discovery: Agent Descriptors, Capability Ontology, and Two-Plane Discovery

abstract.t: Defines how agents describe themselves (AgentDescriptor), the governed capability ontology that makes descriptions comparable, and a two-plane discovery system: a stable plane of signed, content-addressed descriptors indexed in a Kademlia DHT with hot-key sharding, and a volatile plane of on-demand status queries and optional scoped presence gossip. Also specifies bootstrap, the NAT-traversal profile, and discovery privacy.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document family are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here. No adaptation or weakening of these terms applies.

section.name: Two-plane rationale (normative consequence)
section.t: Stable facts (identity, capabilities, models, transports, pricing policy) change on the order of days; volatile facts (queue depth, free VRAM, current TTFT) change on the order of seconds. Systems that push volatile facts through global storage or gossip fail at scale and route on stale data (critique C3). Therefore:

ul.li: R1: Volatile fields MUST NOT appear in descriptors or DHT records.
R2: Routing decisions requiring volatile facts obtain them by direct

section.t: STATUS_QUERY to a shortlist derived from the stable plane.

ul.li: R3: Latency is measured by the querier, never advertised (critique C6).
R4: Trust/reputation fields MUST NOT appear anywhere in this document's

section.t: structures (critique C1); trust lives in draft-map-trust-01.

section.name: AgentDescriptor
section.t: An out-of-session envelope (msg-type 0x0100), content-addressed by descriptor-cid = multihash(suite-hash, envelope-bytes).

Validation: signature per core §4.3; seq MUST exceed any cached seq for the subject (else stale — keep newer); validity ≤ 24 h; descriptors with trust/latency/load-shaped extension fields SHOULD be treated as non-conformant by public-mesh policy. Model claims are claims; the weights multihash is the only verifiable model identity (TH6) and SHOULD be present for any model whose substitution matters.

section.name: STATUS — the volatile plane
section.t: Reports are hints: self-estimates that later become checkable against receipt evidence (TTFT promised vs. observed — trust §8). Providers MUST rate-limit STATUS_QUERY per core §8.3; queriers SHOULD query ≤10 candidates per routing decision.

section.name: Capability Ontology
section.t: Capabilities are hierarchical URIs under map:cap:; matching is by exact segment prefix (a provider of inference/text-generation/code matches a query for inference/text-generation). Initial branches (registry with Expert Review policy, ops §3):
section.sourcecode: map:cap:inference/text-generation[/code|/chat] map:cap:inference/embedding map:cap:inference/vision | /speech-to-text | /text-to-speech | /image-gen map:cap:tool/git | /shell | /compiler/<lang> | /browser | /sql map:cap:lang/<bcp47-or-programming-language-tag> ; qualifier axis map:cap:memory/<domain> ; retrieval domains map:cap:relay map:cap:gateway/<namespace> ; infrastructure roles map:cap:schedule/reservation ; tasks §6
section.t: Free-text tags MUST NOT be used as DHT keys (critique C12); descriptors MAY carry informative free-text specialties in ExtMap for UI only. Ontology versioning: additions are backward compatible; renames occur only at protocol major versions with alias records.

Gateway provenance (ops §5, rule G-1). A CapEntry MAY carry a params map (CapEntry = {1 => CapURI, ?2 => { * uint => any }}). For the gateway/ branch the following params key is registered (FINAL, immutable — ops §3.3):

tr.td: The fronted capability is re-advertised through this gateway namespace.

section.t: When a gateway advertises a fronted capability (e.g. map:cap:inference/text-generation) it SHOULD attach {1: <namespace>} to that CapEntry, so a consumer sees the capability is proxied. The gateway's descriptor subject remains the gateway's own AgentID — never the upstream (G-1). The wire assignment above is authoritative: the gateway-of params key (FINAL, immutable) is the normative carrier of provenance. A reference-implementation note: the scaffold Descriptor codec does not yet model CapEntry params, so early implementations used an out-of-band GatewayAdvert wrapper; closing that codec gap is a separate, additive task and does not change the wire form specified here.

section.name: Stable-plane publication (DHT)
section.t: Provider records map capability keys to descriptor pointers:
section.sourcecode: K(cap) = multihash(suite-hash, "map:idx:1:" || CapURI) ProviderRecord (signed, out-of-session envelope, ttl <= 6h): { 1 => AgentID, 2 => descriptor-cid, 3 => seq, 4 => Timestamp, ? 5 => [+ tstr] /* addr hints */ }
section.t: Agents publish one record per offered capability (bounded: MUST NOT exceed 32 capability keys; aggregate under parents instead), republish every 1–6 h, and store the full descriptor retrievably at H("map:desc:" || descriptor-cid) and/or serve it on request (CAP_RESPONSE). Rotation/revocation records live under the identity key (identity §7).

Data ownership (normative): the agent is the sole source of truth for its descriptor; DHT provider records and all peer caches are derived data — rebuildable at any time by republication, repairable by re-fetch, and never load-bearing for correctness. Loss or suppression of index records degrades discoverability but cannot corrupt truth (integrity is end-to-end via CID + signature, §8). Conflicts between copies resolve by seq alone — last-writer-wins scoped per subject, with the subject as the only writer.

section.name: Hot-key sharding
section.t: Popular capabilities would concentrate millions of provider records on one DHT neighborhood. Therefore every capability key is sharded 256 ways:
section.sourcecode: shard(agent) = first byte of the DIGEST carried in multihash(suite-hash, AgentID) ; NOT the first byte of the multihash itself, which is the ; constant hash-code prefix and would put every agent in ; one shard K'(cap, s) = multihash(suite-hash, "map:idx:1:" || CapURI || ":" || s)
section.t: In the key preimage, s is rendered as its unpadded base-10 ASCII decimal ("0".."255" — e.g. shard 141 contributes the three bytes 31 34 31), not as a raw byte or hex; the derived-constants test vector K′ fixes this form.

Providers publish only to their own shard K'(cap, shard(agent)). Queriers sample r uniformly random shards (RECOMMENDED r = 3, doubling until enough candidates or r = 16) and merge. Properties: publication load per key drops 256×; sampling yields an unbiased provider sample (useful against TH11 — an adversary must capture many shard neighborhoods to bias results); the shard function is verifiable, so a record found in the wrong shard is discarded.

section.name: CAP_QUERY (direct/relayed query)
section.t: For scoped meshes or privacy, a querier MAY send CAP_QUERY {constraints: CapURI, params, zone, limits} directly to known peers or a rendezvous relay instead of the DHT; peers answer CAP_RESPONSE with descriptor CIDs they can vouch having verified. Constraint fields marked hard (context size, zone, sandbox class) MUST be honored by responders — the normative filter semantics that replace the rejected global score formula (critique C5); ranking of survivors is querier policy.
Content maps (registry assignment; added 2026-07-05 from TASK-006):

The querier verifies every returned envelope (signature + self-signature kid == subject + ttl) before caching; a forged or stale entry is dropped, never cached. Responders SHOULD cap a CAP_RESPONSE at 8 descriptors and set more = true when truncating. (A responder MAY answer with bare descriptor CIDs for a follow-up fetch instead of inline envelopes; this profile inlines the envelopes so a single round-trip yields verifiable descriptors.)

section.name: Anti-eclipse and record integrity
section.t: Queriers MUST use disjoint-path Kademlia lookups (≥3 disjoint paths) for identity and descriptor fetches; DHT routing tables SHOULD enforce IP-prefix diversity per bucket; descriptor integrity is end-to-end (CID + signature), so the DHT is untrusted storage — an eclipse can hide providers (degrade) but cannot forge them. Bootstrap lists MUST support multiple independent sources (static config, DNS TXT under operator domains, cached peers); example.org names are used in examples — .local is reserved by mDNS and MUST NOT appear in public bootstrap configuration (critique C14).

section.name: Discovery privacy
section.t: Options, by increasing cost: (a) shard sampling already hides which providers you saw; (b) route CAP_QUERY via a relay peer (map:cap:relay) stripping the querier's address; (c) decoy queries on unrelated capabilities; (d) Zone-3 ephemeral identity for the whole discovery session. STATUS_QUERY inherently reveals requester→candidate interest; privacy-sensitive requesters SHOULD status-query through the same relay. Residual risks: arch §8.3.

section.name: NAT traversal and reachability profile
section.t: Public-mesh providers MUST support: AutoNAT v2 (reachability self-diagnosis), Circuit Relay v2 (relayed listening when unreachable), DCUtR (hole punching upgrade), and QUIC as first-choice transport. Descriptors list relayed multiaddrs when direct addresses are absent. Relays are ordinary agents advertising map:cap:relay with PricingHint; relayed bytes are ciphertext (arch §5). Mobile/intermittent agents SHOULD set short descriptor validity and rely on RESUME (tasks §8) rather than session persistence.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Descriptor spoofing is prevented by signatures; descriptor flooding by per-peer ingestion rate limits and admission costs (trust §5); stale-record attacks by seq monotonicity; wrong-shard placement by shard verification (§6); eclipse degradation bounded by §8. Fingerprinting surface is bounded by bucket coarseness — implementers MUST NOT add high-entropy optional fields to public descriptors (arch §8.2).

A safe public descriptor carries only the coarse registered fields (cap, pricing, hw-class, sandbox, shard bucket, relayed multiaddrs); two providers in the same bucket are therefore indistinguishable beyond those fields. A leaky descriptor that adds a high-entropy optional field — for example a per-instance device-uuid or a 256-bit random nonce — violates the MUST NOT above: it lets an observer single out one provider across sessions and shards, defeating bucket coarseness. Such optional fields MUST instead travel on the Zone-3 ephemeral identity (§9(d)) or in a direct, mutually-authenticated channel, never in a public descriptor.

section.name: IANA-Style Considerations
section.t: Registries established: MAP Capability Ontology; MAP CapEntry Parameter keys (per branch); MAP HardwareClass code points; MAP Sandbox Classes. The assigned values and the family-wide index are in draft-map-wire-01.md §3.10, §3.11, and §3.12; in case of divergence the normative definitions in §4 and §2 govern.
